messages.subject: Erratic behaviour of packrat in packrat/lib-R folder
parts:
hello, 

I use packrat in severals genomics projects and packrat is very cool to manage the packages associated to the projects. Thanks for this work.

However, I have a technical problem and I can't to identify the cause.

What I do ?: 
1. I install packat and my libraries:

#local library parameters: we use the Packrat package to install a local library in the folder output_path 
packrat::init(output_path)
package for ANNOTATIONanalysis
install.packages("GenomicRanges")
install.packages("AnnotationHub")
install.packages("FDb.InfiniumMethylation.hg19")
install.packages("org.Hs.eg.db")
install.packages("gplots")
2. After I run my R script: it works

3. I quit R

4. because I like to reproduce the results, I rerun my script and when I load my libraries:
        packrat::on(output_path)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(AnnotationHub)
library(FDb.InfiniumMethylation.hg19)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(gplots)

the message error appears: 

> library(GenomicRanges)
Loading required package: BiocGenerics
Loading required package: parallel
Error in library(pkg, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE, lib.loc = lib.loc) :
  âparallelâ is not a valid installed package
> library(AnnotationHub)
Loading required package: IRanges
Loading required package: BiocGenerics
Loading required package: parallel
Error in library(pkg, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE, lib.loc = lib.loc) :
  âparallelâ is not a valid installed package
> library(FDb.InfiniumMethylation.hg19)
Loading required package: GenomicFeatures
Loading required package: BiocGenerics
Loading required package: parallel
Error in library(pkg, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE, lib.loc = lib.loc) :
  âparallelâ is not a valid installed package

5. I check in my packrat folder : packrat/lib-R . the folder is empty and I don't understant why. I have reproduce this problem at leat 10 times and each time, I need to reinstall my localLibraryPackrat

So, may be, I do something wrong. may be, it's bug. But it's certainly problematic.

Thanks to give your reflexion about that and I continue to investigate on my side.

Hi Greg,

Thanks for the bug report. Can you provide a bit more information:

1. Prior to running `packrat::on()`, is that `lib-R` directory populated? (You should see `parallel`, among other packages, in there.)

2. After running `packrat::on()`, is that `lib-R` directory now empty?

3. What is the output of `.libPaths()`

4. If the directory is now empty, does running:

    packrat::on(<projectDir>)
    packrat:::symlinkSystemPackages()
    packrat:::useSymlinkedSystemLibrary()

refresh the `lib-R` path?

I'll see if I can reproduce this locally as well.

Thanks,
Kevin
